paras: The killing of Marshal Smith was the fatal shooting of a Black preacher at his door on Carruthers' plantation at Clinton, Louisiana, on a Thursday night in late January 1882. Two white men, named in the dispatches as McKee and Singlebarre or Singlebury, were arrested for the murder on circumstantial evidence. The case reached the national press only as a brief wire item, and no later report of its outcome was found.

Smith, described as "a colored preacher on Carruthers' plantation," was "called to the door on Thursday night and shot," according to a dispatch dated Clinton, January 31. By the dispatch's own dating, that Thursday would have been January 26. The dispatch did not name the person who fired, describe a motive, or say whether more than one assailant was present.

McKee and Singlebury, "two white men," were arrested "on circumstantial evidence and imprisoned." A New Orleans brief of the same date gave the second man's name as Singlebarre and reported that both had been arrested for Smith's murder. No report of an inquest, indictment or trial appears in the coverage.

The story circulated in two forms on January 31 and February 1: a one-sentence New Orleans brief and a slightly longer Clinton dispatch that added the plantation, the night-time call to the door, and the circumstantial basis for the arrests. The Memphis Public Ledger ran the brief on January 31 under "Arrested for Murdering a Colored Preacher," and the Sacramento Daily Record-Union headed it "Charged with Murder." The Clinton version appeared in the Savannah Morning News as "A Colored Preacher Assassinated," in the Knoxville Daily Chronicle as "A Colored Preacher Killed," and in the Richmond Daily Dispatch as "A Colored Preacher Murdered."

The brief also ran in news digests in the Memphis Daily Appeal, the Wheeling Daily Intelligencer and the Salt Lake Herald on February 1, and in the Daily Evening Bulletin of Kentucky and the Helena Weekly Herald on February 2. Each paper identified the victim as "colored" and the accused as white, but none commented on the case, and the accused's surname was printed in at least six spellings. No report of the killing from a Louisiana paper or from the Black press was found.

accounts.label: Clinton dispatch
accounts.gist: Smith, a colored preacher on Carruthers' plantation, was called to his door Thursday night and shot; McKee and Singlebury were arrested on circumstantial evidence and jailed.

framing.detail: Papers ran the item as a one-line brief or short dispatch under headlines such as 'Charged with Murder' and 'A Colored Preacher Assassinated', without comment.

conflicts.note: Wire copy also printed Singleburry, Singleberry, Singlebarry and 'Single Cary' (one paper gave 'V. McKee'); these are transmission or typesetting variants of one name, and the correct spelling cannot be settled from these texts.
Two reprints spelled the name 'Marshall' and one printed 'Michael Smith'; the two fullest reports agree on Marshal.
